ishikawa.comment: Read the beta header before the stable-header fallback. ishikawa.md#units-and-contexts: 2. `ishikawa-beta`, then `ishikawa`, case-insensitively, are `header` units. A header unit must not be followed by a word character. The beta form is tried first. Thus `ishikawa-betaX`, `ishikawa-beta1`, and `ishikawa-beta_` start with the stable header and have node text beginning `-beta`; `ishikawa-beta-x` uses the beta header and begins its text at `-x`.

patterns.comment: Read a native comment only at a unit start; preserve directives in padding and content. ishikawa.md#units-and-contexts: 1. After zero or more whitespace characters, `%%` starts a diagram comment. Its body is the longest run before a line break, U+2028, U+2029, or the end of text. The whitespace before its marker is trivia. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read node text as an unquoted label; preserve directives and stop before a common comment. ishikawa.md#units-and-contexts: 5. `node-text` is one or more characters other than a line break, read as far as possible. It includes internal whitespace, U+2028 and U+2029, punctuation, quotes, backticks, backslashes, NUL, U+0085, and U+200B. U+0085 and U+200B are text even at the start; they are not indentation. There is no quoted-string context and no escape syntax. ishikawa.md#units-and-contexts: Once `node-text` has begun, a header spelling, `%%`, and an unselected `;` remain part of that text. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.mermaid
